I would also just quickly draw attention to Article 4 which notes that the assembly of the community and its bodies would continue to work as the assembly of the autonomous region and its bodies. So in effect, the association of municipalities of Bosnian Krajina changed its name and its stature, so to speak, into the Autonomous Region of Krajina as an inseparable part of the federal state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Autonomous Region of Krajina adopted a statute on the same day, did they not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. They also have a statute, and it is almost identical to the preceding statute of the community of municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that is, for Your Honours, Exhibit P80. I don't think we will trouble you taking you to that statute. Could the witness be shown Exhibit P22? Mr. Treanor, did Radoslav Brdjanin continue to play an important role?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. As indicated in the decision that I just read, he continued to be the first vice-president of the assembly and he continued to play an active role in that assembly, in the affairs of the now so-called Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document that you have in front of you is dated the 29th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document purports to be a telex to be delivered to the mayor?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, this document is apparently a telex sent by Radoslav Brdjanin signing as vice-president of the assembly of the autonomous region and coordinator for the carrying out of decisions, and it refers to a meeting of all presidents of assemblies held on the 26th of October, 1991, under the leadership of Dr. Radovan Karadzic, the president of the SDS, and a decision which was adopted at that meeting and endorsed, accepted, at a session again reference to the Presidency of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and the government of the autonomous region, and the document itself refers to the issue of mobilisation, ordering the formation of command posts in item number 1, mobilisation of the Territorial Defence in item number 2, and in item number 5, goes on, for instance, to specify the taking of authority in public enterprises, the postal service and the social accountancy service, banks and courts.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown a new document? It is an intercept dated the 31st of October, 1991. This is an intercept between Radovan Karadzic and Radoslav Brdjanin. Disclosure number 2.460. If that can be provisionally marked P2357?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly, what is the context of the conversation about?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, this is a record of a telephone conversation between Radoslav Brdjanin and Radovan Karadzic on the 31st of October, 1991, which is a few days after the meeting of the 26th of October that was referred to in the previous document and a couple of days after that document was sent out, Brdjanin calls Karadzic to discuss various problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just -- I just want to make a record objection with regard to this and the other intercepts that have been mentioned today, that they all significantly predate the parameters of the indictment in this case, which is 1992. This one we are clear back in October of 1991. I suggest that it's not relevant and should not be admitted or alluded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Your objection is not being sustained Mr. Ackerman. I have read the intercept, both this one and the previous one. There is information there or facts that may have relevance with respect to the period which is covered then by the indictment, particularly with regard to the powers that according to Karadzic himself, your client had in the political arena at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, let me just also say for the record, then, Your Honour, that the powers he had in October, 1991 have no relationship to the powers he might have had during the term of the indictment. That would be my argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. But your objection is not being sustained because the Trial Chamber still thinks that at this point in time this is an open matter and we need to get all the information we require to see exactly what your client's position, political and -- within the political structure was, starting from 1991, because that is relevant for the 1992 period. Yes, Mr. Treanor, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, Mr. Brdjanin called Dr. Karadzic to discuss various problems he was having in the Krajina region, and is going to Karadzic to seek some decisions on some of these issues, and Karadzic is a little bit impatient and says --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Not a little bit. He was quite impatient.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At one point in the conversation, which I want to point out, which is at the bottom of page 4 of the translation, where Karadzic says to Brdjanin, "Call me about something that you cannot resolve. You have all the power in Krajina. Why don't you exercise this power?" And at the bottom of that page, Karadzic says -- the translation here is a little different from the way I would render this. Karadzic says, "If Brdjo, if Stojan Zupljanin is no good, replace them." So he's encouraging his -- Brdjanin to take charge of the situation there.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I think I've finished with that document. If the witness could be shown Exhibit P23? This is an extract from the minutes of the 9th session of the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina -- of a session held on the 6th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, this is an extract from the actual record of the session. That is a document that was drawn up after the session and reflects what actually did happen at the session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the bottom of the item 1 is the implementation of conclusions adopted at the session and does it state at the bottom of item 1, it was decided that the vice-president of the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, Radoslav Brdjanin, should inform the president of the Bosnia-Herzegovina SDS, Radovan Karadzic, as to the implementation of the conclusions adopted at the session of the assembly of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, that is what it says, and as the Court will recall, the document of the 29th of October was signed by Brdjanin as the coordinator for the carrying out of decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The document was not signed at all. It was a telex so there was no signature so that's a misstatement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman is correct and in fact at the bottom, at the end of the document, there is also another name. I don't know whose it is but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, let me rephrase that, in that document, Mr. Brdjanin is described as the coordinator for the carrying out of decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And here he's being asked to report on the carrying out of those decisions to Radovan Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I meant is this: That perhaps you can enlighten us on -- leave it. You have explained it enough. That's okay. No problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, also at the end of the discussion of item 2, which is on mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, there is a discussion on that issue and, again, Radoslav Brdjanin is designated by the assembly to play a role in that connection. On the last page of the translation, just above the middle of the page, at the -- just above where item 3 begins, it's -- the record states that "In the end it was decided that on behalf of the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, Vojo Kupresanin, Vojo Maksimovic, Aleksa Buha and Radoslav Brdjanin should request that the SFRY Presidency declare a state of war and that the number of commanding officers of Serbian nationality on the front be in proportion to the number of Serbian conscripts on the front."

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness be shown a new document, this is another intercept dated the 7th of January, 1992, disclosure number 2.538. This is an intercept between Radovan Karadzic and Miroslav, if that could be provisionally marked P2358?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly before we break, this is quite a lengthy telephone conversation but could you briefly tell the Court the context of the conversation and then what is important in this conversation? Or what is of interest in this conversation?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Well, this is a conversation between Radovan Karadzic and a certain Miroslav who is apparently one of the local politicians from Bosnian Krajina, about the situation in that area, and they get around to discussing some of the personalities involved and the type of people that are required, and the name of Radoslav Brdjanin comes up in a favourable manner, Miroslav telling Karadzic at one point, after Karadzic says - which I'm trying to locate in the translation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it towards the bottom of page 7 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, I was -- I had skipped this. I haven't read it. I would suggest that we have the break now so that it gives me the opportunity to read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I would like to know the content of this intercept. So we will have a 25 minute break again starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, before we broke, we were -- you were just about to briefly advise the Chamber of the content of the conversation of the intercept between Radovan Karadzic and Miroslav on the 7th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, as I believe I said this is a conversation involving a -- one of the local politicians from the Bosnian Krajina consulting with Karadzic on problems in that area, particularly personnel problems in the assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. One of the main topics of conversation is the position of Andjelko Grahovac, who is the president of what they now call the government of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, apparently Grahovac called Karadzic to tell him that there was some sort of inquiry going on about him and Karadzic asks Miroslav about this, on page 3 of the translation, in the middle, Miroslav replies, in relation to a Grahovac, he should go. Karadzic says, "But he said he didn't want anyone to attack him, therefore maybe someone could suggest that he resign." Miroslav: "To suggest a resignation?" Karadzic: "Yes, yes, some of the people, he's -- the liaison officer between you and him should suggest that he resign." Miroslav: "They are now trying to back out of this in every possible way. That's completely natural, you know, because, we then found out that Vojo was spoken ill of in Belgrade. They are speaking ill of everyone they can think of." Karadzic: "Yes, yes." Miroslav: "Speaking ill." Karadzic: "They are speaking ill of Brdjanin as well." Miroslav: "Come on, Brdjo has nothing to do with this. He was away for two months chasing his nephew around the battlefield. The man was not in Celinac at all." They then go on to continue discussing the issue of Grahovac and his position in the middle of page 4 of the translation, we see Karadzic suggesting, "All right, I mean, if it can be done with no drama and resignations rather than without any argumentation, then that's better if possible, and do you -- who would be the second premier designate?" Miroslav: "Well, I think that one is from Kupres, I don't know, I don't remember the name, but I think, just a moment, someone called Herceg from Kupres." Karadzic: "Uh-huh, what's he like?" Miroslav: "Well, they say he's good." Karadzic: "Where does he live?" Miroslav: "He lives there but since this is professional I think it would be good if he were here. But I don't think that he will. I think that the main people are Dr. Jaksic and Brdjanin. It will most probably be one of them." Karadzic: "Dr. Jaksic?" Miroslav: "Yes." Karadzic: "What's he like?" "Well he would cooperate well with Radic and the other municipalities. He's more of a scientist and he would set out everything on economic grounds." Karadzic: "Don't give us a scientist, don't." Miroslav: "Yes, yes." Karadzic: "Give us a political figure who will be able to take power." Miroslav: "Then it would have to be Brdjanin, I think." And they continue the discussion and I would just point out finally on page 6 of the translation, towards the top of the page, Karadzic says to Miroslav, "Go ahead, choose a mature personality, one that is politically strong and will be able to create -- and be able to create." Miroslav: "Tell me, you know what, I think that Brdjanin, but Brdjanin is, how can I explain it a bit rash." Karadzic: "All right but he's the vice-chairman of the assembly it would be difficult for him to --" Miroslav: "Yes. But I don't know how they plan to do it." Karadzic: "Yes, then he'd have to leave the assembly and someone else would have to be elected to the assembly." Miroslav: "Any way, any way, yes, someone would have to be, so would you -- would you perhaps speak to Vojo and Brdjanin?" Karadzic: "Please, please, you call them. Call them and tell them to discuss things. I think that Jaksic is not appropriate at this moment because -- because a person with political would suit you better now." "Strong politically, yes." "Excuse me for a moment. Hello is that --" and they -- and the situation continues. So this conversation indicates that Brdjanin was being considered as a replacement for Grahovac in the position of chairman of the executive committee.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Mr. Treanor. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I was waiting for Mr. Treanor to finish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is the explanation the same as before, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, I think so Your Honour because I was going to raise the same thing. Mr. Treanor and my copies are obviously different as well so I think he's got the earlier translation but I will check that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND

utterances.text: So it's the one which we were given this morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JANU
utterances.text: We have ET.

utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.text: All right. That's for the record, and you can take it -- yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.text: Does ET then -- I'm glad to know that. As I understand it, then, ET means it was done by someone in the Office of Prosecutor rather than CLSS? Am I correct about that?

utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour -- yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.text: Thank you very much, it's been a while.

utterances.text: Yes, thank you. So I will be cautious in saying which of the two versions I will ask my two colleagues to rely upon later on. Point taken, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we will undertake to have them rechecked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am sure you will, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: The ones we have used this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I am sure you will. So let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown a new document which was part of disclosure 2.214? It's dated the 21st of November, 1991 and it was the decision on the verification of the proclaimed Serbian autonomous districts in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I want to deal now with further developments with respect to the regions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if that can be marked provisionally P2359?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think this is not the correct document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: ERN number 0044-8160.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: You're referring to the 21 November, 1991 decision on the verification?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Not that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My document has highlighting of the municipalities, and one line under section 2, if that can go on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I have is 2.214 is an article from Kozarski Vjesnik of 9 October, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Ms. Gustin just advised me of the same thing, Your Honour. I was given this exhibit number yesterday as this document being a part of, and I must say, I didn't go back to the actual exhibit binder and take it from there. I printed it out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In any event, the document is on the ELMO machine. Now I don't have my copy. Can you just explain for the Court this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, this document is a decision passed by the Bosnian Serb assembly on the 21st of November, 1991. I would just observe that the Bosnian Serb assembly as described in section 3 of our main report was established on the 24th of October, 1991, from the deputies club of the SDS, and that at this time in November, indeed until the end of December, it was the only central governmental-type body of the Bosnian Serbs, that is the -- they had at that point no executive council, council of ministers, government, whatever you want to call it, and no Presidency. By this decision, the Bosnian Serb assembly recognises the proclamation of the Serbian autonomous districts and the Serbian -- and the Autonomous Region of Krajina, basically giving them its imprimatur. At the top of section 1 of the decision, it mentions the Autonomous Region of Krajina first and mentions the municipalities and other areas that would compose the Autonomous Region of Krajina, with its seat in Banja Luka. It then goes on to enumerate the other Serbian autonomous districts and their composition. I would also draw attention to item number 2, in which the Bosnian Serb Assembly defines the Serbian autonomous region, that is the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and the districts, described above, as federal units in the joint state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see in item 1 the reference to Bosanska Krupa in the -- as one of the municipalities?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, the municipalities are enumerated under their geographical appellation, Kljuc, Kotor Varos, et cetera. When we get to Bosanska Krupa, it refers, however, to the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa, as well as parts of the municipality of Donji Vakuf and other municipalities in this region that have a Serbian majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you be shown another document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And Your Honours and the Defence it's part of disclosure 2.414, not 2.214. I apologise for the mistake. Can that be provisionally marked P2360? And that is a decision on the -- sorry, a recommendation on establishing municipal assemblies of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina dated the 11th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain for the Court this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes. This document is a -- another resolution passed by the Bosnian Serb assembly, this time on the 11th of December, 1991. It's entitled a recommendation on the foundation of assemblies of municipalities of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Basically what it does in paragraph 1 of the recommendation is that it calls on the clubs of assemblymen, the SDS clubs of assemblymen in the municipal assemblies to found a separate Serbian assembly in those municipalities in which they are outvoted by the other members of the municipal assembly, resulting in, as it puts it in paragraph 1, the imposition by majority vote of decisions contrary to the interests of the Serbian people. The final paragraph of the decision instructs the -- that the decisions passed by the SDS clubs of assemblymen in the municipalities on the transformation of their -- of those clubs into assemblies of the Serbian people be verified by the assembly -- the main assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour I just want to point out for the record that we don't have this document. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just asking Ms. Gustin to check when it was disclosed. The whole range, which covers about 30 pages, because it's an Official Gazette, was disclosed to the Defence on the 26th of October, 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is -- I understand it -- part of the Official Gazette that we had occasion to visit on previous occasions, I suppose, but I would leave it to you to check on that, Mr. Ackerman, and if you still believe that you don't have it, we'll try and find a solution. Thanks. Let's proceed, Ms. Sutherland. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, have you finished with that document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: If I may be permitted to remark that this document, taken together with the previous document, are interesting in that they indicate something about the goals of the Serbian Democratic Party and the Bosnian Serb leadership at this time. As I indicated a little earlier, by this point in time, the SDS leadership had created an assembly, a Bosnian-Serb assembly, a so-called assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina, based on the SDS club of deputies in the assembly -- in the regular assembly of Bosnia-Herzegovina. With the decision on the verification of the autonomous regions, this assembly seems to be attempting to give itself a territory. The autonomous regions, however, were composed, as we saw in the case of the Autonomous Region of Krajina and its preceding community of municipalities of Banja Luka, were composed of municipalities which chose to join those institutions. Now, that would in principle only have been municipalities in which the SDS had a political majority in the assemblies of those municipalities. The recommendation on establishing assemblies of municipalities of the Serbian people indicates a desire to take particular portions of municipalities, which are not as a whole, which do not as a whole have a Serbian majority and establish them as separate municipalities, which could then join one of the autonomous regions. Indeed, in the decision on verification we mention the fact that in paragraph 1 it already mentions a Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa. So I just want to point out that what I think is going on here by way of establishing autonomous regions as a territorial base for the SDS and the recommendation as an attempt to expand that territorial base into municipalities which were not Serbian majority municipalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I ask you to look at another document, a new document? Which consists of five separate documents within the one document. I must say, the covering letter, a different version of this covering letter, I think, is Exhibit P2162, if my memory serves me correctly. And this has ERN number SA 00-9048. If it can be provisionally marked P2361?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor just quickly, can we see there --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: If it's already P1 -- 2162, why does it have to have a new number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, without giving evidence, that letter is addressed to the SDA, this letter is addressed to Momcilo Krajisnik. It was the same bundle of documents that were provided to both the SDA and to Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the President, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's perfectly in order, Mr. Ackerman. I would have understood and even agreed with your remark, but as it is, I think it needs to be given a separate exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, the next question is: What is the -- I see you've given me an ERN number. If I look at this ERN number, do you think that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know what you have there so I can't help you there, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This bundle was provided yesterday, I understand, but the other document was disclosed a long time ago, the covering letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, can you very briefly tell the Court what these documents are about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, can we have it on the ELMO as well, please? Thank you, Madam usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This is a package of material that was sent with a covering letter on the 18th of December, 1991, from the assembly of the Serbian people of Bosanska Krupa to Momcilo Krajisnik. Attached to the letter are five separate items, including a decision, item number 4, on the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, the document he's describing has nothing -- no relationship at all to P2162. P2162 is dated 19 June of 1992 and talks about supplying potable water and fire brigade tanker trucks.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I did say if my memory serves me correctly. I will have Ms. Gustin look up the exact exhibit number for Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ackerman, and Ms. Gustin is checking that but in any case, we are dealing with the exhibit that we have on the ELMO and perhaps we can proceed on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Treanor.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: This material apparently was sent to Momcilo Krajisnik as the chairman, as the president of the assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia-Herzegovina pursuant to the recommendation that that assembly made on the 11th of December basically informing that assembly in accordance with the last paragraph of the recommendation that a Serbian assembly of Bosanska Krupa had indeed been established. One other feature of these documents which I would draw the Court's attention to is contained in paragraph 2, which I believe is the next page in the translation of the decision on the verification of the proclaimed Serbian assembly of Bosanska Krupa, in which it states that the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa is part of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Similarly, in paragraph 2 of the decision on the proclamation of the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa, which I believe is two pages further on in the translation, it says, in the translation incorrectly but in a similar fashion to the other document, that the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa is part of the autonomous region, of what it calls the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka, the reference obviously being to the Autonomous Region of Krajina which is what the translation indicates, although in the original it refers to the Autonomous Region of Banja Luka. So a new municipality at this stage has definitely joined the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And joined it on the 11th of December, 1991, and we saw in Exhibit P2359, dated the 21st of November, that the Serbian municipality of Bosanska Krupa was actually named in that document, did we not?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for Your Honours and Mr. Ackerman, the exhibit number of the same document going to the SDA is P2061. I apologise for giving you the wrong exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you check that, Mr. Ackerman, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I have a copy here. 2061.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'm sorry, one thing I forgot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, one moment, I understand Ms. Korner you require about five minutes. Mr. Ackerman do you require.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you require any -- do you have any points, matters to raise before we close down for the day today or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just very briefly with regard to this situation we are having today regarding documents. I just want to make an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We need to hand down an oral decision very briefly, one minute on the 22nd and 23rd protective measures because that has become urgent now. So I would suggest, Ms. Sutherland, that you adjust the amount of questions that you still have left according to the importance, leaving us something like five minutes, five to six or seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I will do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor, I'm sorry, one thing I meant to ask you this morning as we were going through your work experience and qualifications, when did you first learn to read the -- what's commonly known as the Serbo-Croat language?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: I began studying Serbo Croatian, as it was then called, in 1970. I had previously studied the Russian language for many years, as well as Bulgarian, and I began studying Serbo Croatian as my third Slavic language in 1970.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: All right. I finished with that document. Could the witness be shown another document which is disclosure 2.46? With the ERN number 0044-8167. It's a decision on the establishment and election of the ministerial council of the Assembly of the Serbian People in Bosnia and Herzegovina, dated the 21st of December, 1991. It's part of the Official Gazette of the 15th of January -- published on the 15th of January, 1992. Your Honour, this document has a different ERN number to the one I just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have it as disclosure 2.414 with the ERN number she gave. I assume this is the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: This is yet another version of it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Treanor --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If that could be provisionally marked just the decision on the establishment as P2362?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please briefly tell the Court the significance of this document?

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. As I mentioned earlier, the Bosnian Serb Assembly had been established in October -- 24th October, 1991, and was the only organ of the -- central organ of the Bosnian Serbs until this time. This decision marks a development in their governing structure. The assembly forms what it calls a council of ministers by this decision on the 21st of December and it specifies who the members are. I would quickly draw attention to two names. In paragraph 2, after the list of 18 names, those 18 names being basically SDS office-holders in the government of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, occupying corresponding ministries in the new Bosnian Serb council of ministers. Below that list we see a list of additional names which are the names of the presidents of the governments of the Serbian autonomous regions, including in item number 20, Andjelko Grahovac the president of the government of what it calls here the Serbian autonomous district of Bosnian Krajina, as ex officio members of that government. Then I would also draw attention to item number 17 in paragraph 3 where it mentions the name of Jovan Cizmovic, as a minister without portfolio in that council of ministers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In that very next decision in that same Official Gazette, very quickly, on the 21st of December, 1991, it's a decision on the appointment of the coordinators of the governments and executive bodies of the Serbian autonomous districts and the Autonomous Region of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: PATRICK TREANOR
utterances.text: Yes, well this document, which is passed by the assembly on the same day, we get to find out what the significance of Jovan Cizmovic is precisely and he has been named to be coordinator for the work of the executive organs of the Serbian autonomous districts and the Autonomous Region of Krajina, a position which the previous document indicates was important enough to get him named as a minister without portfolio in the council of ministers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: This second document that's number 23 in the gazette, does it have the same exhibit number P2362 or are you giving it a separate exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good point, Ms. Sutherland. I don't know how to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It can have a separate Exhibit number P2362.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sorry, P2363.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P2363. We don't have it, at least to my knowledge, Madam Registrar, neither this one nor the previous one. Sir, before you leave this courtroom, we need this because you will be cross-examined at a later stage, there is one part in your report which you were referred to earlier on today, namely section 5, which was authored by Xavier Aguirre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It was included in your report.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you assume responsibility for it without reservations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You do. All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, we intend to continue with Mr. Treanor tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. But I wanted to make this clear because it's very important. I mean I do not think you are producing Mr. Aguirre as a witness, are you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour for the simple reason we are trying to keep the witness count down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I can live with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I put it this way? If there is any serious challenge to what is effectively an analysis of what the documents show, then we will put him in to be cross-examined by Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a possibility as well that we may also require Mr. Treanor to come back later on. So we leave it at that for today. I thank you, sir, for being patient with us. We'll see you again tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman, I think in order not to waste time or lose time --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour, I just want to, for the record, and as a very practical matter object very strongly to the proposition that documents are for the first time brought before the witness even though they may have been given to us last night, brought before the witness and the witness is commenting on them. I don't have them. No opportunity to read them. There may be valid objections that I could make to the use of the document. I can't possibly tell if I can't read it and I just think that's an inappropriate way to present evidence in this Trial Chamber and those documents should have been disclosed to us well before yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you want to respond to that, Ms. Sutherland?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I will do it. Your Honour the difficulty has been that we have had to speed everything up. We never intended to put Mr. Treanor in at this stage of the game, as it were, and so we apologise but the fact is we've been trying to keep it as short and as efficient as possible but Mr. Ackerman's point is taken and we'll try to ensure that it doesn't happen with Mr. Brown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he's right and I appreciate also the problems that you encountered. And I leave all options open, as I have always done. But I appreciate what you say, Ms. Korner. Ms. Korner, I understand that you have got something for to us raise.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just ask to go into private session very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, let's go into private session.
